venue_note: Venue-specific criteria, score scales and AI-use policies (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, CVPR, AAAI, ...) are NOT built in. Supply the current call/review form via rubric.source_file; the system never fills scales from model memory.

criteria.name: Evaluation rigour
criteria.description: Benchmarks, splits, metrics, baselines and statistics allow the stated empirical conclusions.

criteria.name: Attribution of gains
criteria.description: Improvements are attributed to the components that cause them.

criteria.name: Limitations and responsible research
criteria.description: Limitations, licences, societal impact and compute are reported honestly.

checks.name: Evaluation protocol
questions: Are train/validation/test splits standard or fully described? Was the test set used for model selection, early stopping, prompt selection or hyper-parameter tuning?
Are metrics defined precisely (averaging: macro/micro/weighted; top-k; normalisation; which split; which checkpoint)?
Are all compared methods evaluated under the same protocol (same split, same preprocessing, same metric implementation)?
Does the benchmark actually measure the capability claimed (construct validity)?
must_not: Do not assume test-set tuning without textual evidence; if unclear, raise a clarification question.

checks.name: Baseline fairness
questions: Are the strongest and most recent relevant baselines included, including simple/strong baselines (e.g. tuned linear probe, kNN, larger plain model, well-prompted LLM)?
Do baselines get comparable tuning budget, data, pre-training, model size and compute? Are baseline numbers re-run or copied from papers with different settings?
For copied numbers: do task, dataset version, split, input information, supervision, resources and metric definition match?
evidence_needed: quotes describing baseline sources and tuning
must_not: Copying public baseline numbers is not misconduct; state the comparability limitation instead.
Incomparable numbers are background, not proof the method is worse.

checks.name: Ablation and attribution
questions: When the proposed method also changes data size, training budget, teacher model, pre-training data or tuning effort, is the gain isolated for the new component?
Does each claimed component have an ablation under otherwise identical settings (check the appendix before concluding it is missing)?
evidence_needed: quotes of what changed between conditions
ablation table quote or the place it should be
must_not: Confounded comparisons support 'attribution not isolated', never 'the component is ineffective'.

checks.name: Statistical evidence
questions: How many seeds/runs? Are variance, standard error or confidence intervals reported, and over what (seeds, data splits, prompts)?
Are small differences (e.g. < 1 point) presented as improvements without uncertainty?
Are multiple-comparison or cherry-picking risks (best of many runs/prompts/checkpoints) addressed?
evidence_needed: quotes of run counts and reported spread
must_not: Never compute p-values or CIs without the necessary data.
'Evidence insufficient to show significance' differs from 'not significant'.

checks.name: Leakage and contamination
questions: Can test information reach training (duplicates across splits, temporal leakage, subject/patient/user overlap, preprocessing fitted on all data, label leakage via features)?
For pre-trained or foundation models: could the evaluation data be in the pre-training corpus? Is contamination analysed?
evidence_needed: quotes of data collection, deduplication and split procedures
must_not: A plausible leakage route is a clarification question unless the text shows it happened.

checks.name: Scope and generalisation of claims
questions: Do 'state-of-the-art', 'general', 'robust', 'scales' or 'any domain' claims match the number and diversity of datasets, model sizes and settings evaluated?
Are failure cases and negative results reported?
must_not: Propose a scoped rewording rather than calling the result wrong.

checks.name: Reproducibility and compute
questions: Are hyper-parameters, search spaces, seeds, hardware, training time/GPU-hours, parameter counts and inference cost reported for the method and baselines?
Are code, checkpoints and data (or access instructions and licences) promised or provided?
must_not: Missing compute details are usually minor unless efficiency is a core claim.

checks.name: Limitations, licences and impact
questions: Are limitations discussed honestly? Are dataset/model licences, personal data and potential misuse addressed where relevant?
must_not: Do not invent venue policy requirements; cite the supplied rubric/policy if one exists.

subfield_checks.name: LLM evaluation validity
questions: Are model versions/snapshots, decoding parameters (temperature, top-p, max tokens) and prompts (incl. few-shot exemplars) fully reported?
Do baselines receive equal prompt-engineering effort? Is sensitivity to prompt wording reported?
If LLM-as-a-judge is used: which judge, what rubric, any agreement with humans, position/length/self-preference bias controls?
For closed APIs: is non-determinism and model drift addressed? Is benchmark contamination of the evaluated models discussed?
evidence_needed: quotes of prompts/decoding settings or their absence
must_not: Do not assert contamination happened without evidence; ask for analysis.

subfield_checks.name: Agent evaluation
questions: Do all agents get the same tools, environment version, step/token budget and number of attempts (pass@k vs pass@1)?
Is cost (tokens, API spend, wall time) reported alongside success rate? Could the environment leak the answer (e.g. tests visible, internet access)?

subfield_checks.name: Vision / multimodal protocol
subfield_checks.name_zh: 视觉与多模态评测协议
questions: Are resolution, augmentation, pre-training data, backbone and test-time augmentation matched across compared methods?
For generative models: are FID/CLIP-score style metrics computed with the same reference set, sample count and implementation? Are human evaluations described (raters, protocol)?

subfield_checks.name: RL evaluation
questions: How many seeds, and is variability (e.g. IQM, CIs, performance profiles) reported? Are environment versions, frame/step budgets and evaluation episodes consistent across methods?
Are hyper-parameters tuned per environment for the proposed method only?

subfield_checks.name: Learning-theory assumptions
questions: Are assumptions (convexity, smoothness, bounded gradients, i.i.d., realisability, width/limits) stated and realistic for the experiments claimed to illustrate the theory?
Do the bounds/rates claimed in the abstract match the theorem statements, including constants and dependence on dimension or sample size?
must_not: A gap in a proof is 'insufficient argument', not 'false theorem'.

subfield_checks.name: Graph learning protocol
questions: Are transductive/inductive settings, split seeds and feature/label leakage across nodes or edges handled consistently?
